after.summary: Tandem Diabetes Care, Inc. ( Tandem ) has identified that certain Tandem Mobi insulin pumps may generate false-positive occlusion alarms when no actual insulin flow obstruction is present. Investigation determined that increased friction within the drive module can reduce available motor power and, under certain conditions, cause motor speed to fall below the occlusion detection threshold. As a result, the pump may incorrectly detect an occlusion condition and suspend insulin delivery. When an occlusion alarm occurs, insulin delivery remains suspended until the user acknowledges the alarm and resumes therapy. Repeated false-positive occlusion alarms, if not addressed promptly, may result in interruptions of insulin delivery that can increase the risk of elevated blood glucose levels. In severe cases, hyperglycemia may require medical intervention or hospitalization. Product: Tandem Mobi Insulin Pump, Models: 1004004, 1010750, 1012676, 1012719, 1013655, 1013656, 1013501, 1013700, 1014081, 1014801, 1014811, 1014813, 1014936, 1016911, 1016912, 1016913, 1016914, 1018075, 1018077, 1018078 Status: Ongoing.

( Tandem ) has identified that certain Tandem Mobi insulin pumps may generate false-positive occlusion alarms when no actual insulin flow obstruction is present. Investigation determined that increased friction within the drive module can reduce available motor power and, under certain conditions, cause motor speed to fall below the occlusion detection threshold. As a result, the pump may incorrectly detect an occlusion condition and suspend insulin delivery. When an occlusion alarm occurs, insulin delivery remains suspended until the user acknowledges the alarm and resumes therapy. Repeated false-positive occlusion alarms, if not addressed promptly, may result in interruptions of insulin delivery that can increase the risk of elevated blood glucose levels. In severe cases, hyperglycemia may require medical intervention or hospitalization. after.summary: Tandem Diabetes Care, Inc. ( Tandem ) has identified that certain Tandem Mobi insulin pumps may generate false-positive occlusion alarms when no actual insulin flow obstruction is present. Investigation determined that increased friction within the drive module can reduce available motor power and, under certain conditions, cause motor speed to fall below the occlusion detection threshold. As a result, the pump may incorrectly detect an occlusion condition and suspend insulin delivery. When an occlusion alarm occurs, insulin delivery remains suspended until the user acknowledges the alarm and resumes therapy. Repeated false-positive occlusion alarms, if not addressed promptly, may result in interruptions of insulin delivery that can increase the risk of elevated blood glucose levels. In severe cases, hyperglycemia may require medical intervention or hospitalization. after.summary: Retrospective review of servicing records identified AIC units requiring various hardware, firmware, and/or software update(s): 1. RFID firmware issue that may result in failure of the AIC to recognize the purge cassette during case setup or cassette change. This issue may result in delay in procedure or therapy. 2. Potential for the rotary push button (RPB) sticking and unreliable actuation impacting operator ability to select and confirm menu entries. This can result in loss of control of the console. 3. Potential AIC instability that could result in AIC start-up failure, inability to drive the pump, and the need for console exchange. 4. Software defect related to calculator process crash, leading to Negative Central Venous Pressure (CVP) values present in Pulmonary Artery Pressure (PAP) calculations. Product: Automated Impella Controller, Packaged. Primary user control interface for the Impella Catheter, catheter-based heart pump. Status: Ongoing.
